problems: The card never states the core rule: notify inline (synchronously) when the sender belongs to the current thread, and defer only when it lives in another thread. Saying the notification 'can be posted' leaves room to always post. Reviewer 15 noted that same-thread disconnects must still produce a notification right away (e.g. QDBusAbstractInterface relies on getting one), and the final commit keeps the inline path explicitly.

The card omits Reviewer 15's request to document why reading senderPriv is not racy. The connection mutex keeps the sender alive only as far as QObject; it does not stop the destruction of further-derived classes. That is exactly why the virtual calls must be deferred, and the reviewer asked for it to be written into the code docs.

The card leaves out the reviewer's question about the other disconnectNotify call site in qobject.cpp (around line 3630). All in-qtbase paths that call disconnectNotify or resolve the signal on a possibly-foreign sender need checking, not just ~QObject().

The card does not mention the reported regression: this change triggered a crash in Qt CoAP (QTBUG-149883). Deferred, asynchronous disconnectNotify changes behavior for overriders, and the engineer should know that subclasses may break.

The third bullet misframes the out-of-qtbase users. Reviewer 15 only asked whether QObjectPrivate's helper (qobject_p.h) should change and whether QtQml needs a similar fix; that question was left to the QtQml owner and is outside this qtbase change. The card turns it into a qtbase documentation requirement tied to those callers. The actual documentation suggestion was about when disconnectNotify() is called inline versus from the sender's event loop.
